subject: Alpha Health: execution trajectory, subprocessor lineage and export-path evidence
messages:
From: Jane Park <jane.park@alphahealth.co>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q — where do requests actually execute?

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — Alpha Health is excited about the latency and cost numbers. Our security team has one follow-up: for compliance we need a concise explanation of where LLM inference requests execute (regions and any third parties involved). Specifically:

- For requests coming from our east-coast app users, which regions are used by default?
- Which subprocessors could touch request payloads (even transiently) and in what order?
- Are there any cross-border hops we should flag for our legal/IT teams?

Can you provide something I can pass to our security reviewer (ideally a short narrative + a simple inventory)? If possible a map or a CSV of subprocessors would help.

Appreciate it — Jane

Jane Park
Head of IT, Alpha Health
jane.park@alphahealth.co
+1 (415) 555-0199

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q — where do requests actually execute?

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear list. I'm putting Marissa (security) on this thread to provide the technical inventory and a concise explanation we can share with your reviewer.

High level answer for immediate use: by default requests from east-coast users are routed to our US-East execution pool (primary run in us-east-1 region). We maintain a registry of approved subprocessors (cloud/edge partners, monitoring) — most touches are transient (TCP handoffs, autoscaler control plane) and we can provide evidence for each. If you need a formal attestation we can attach the subprocessors CSV and a short diagram.

I'll hand over to Marissa for the technical breakdown and the CSV.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick Q — where do requests actually execute? (internal)

Kim / Connor — drafting the short inventory for Jane. Draft outline below; please flag omissions: 

1) Default routing: us-east-1 (primary). Failover: us-west-2 then eu-west-1 if regional policy requires.

2) Subprocessor chain (typical request path, top-to-bottom):
   - Customer frontend (Alpha Health app) -> VPC NAT -> edge LB (partner: FastEdge CDN) [transient] -> Redwood API gateway (hosted control plane in us-east-1)
   - Serving runtime: hosted GPUs (our Dedicated pools or hosted variant) run in cloud provider accounts we manage; compute instances are provisioned in us-east-1.
   - Observability/telemetry: internal telemetry agents push anonymized metrics to Datadog (managed) — no raw payload retained.
   - Billing/usage: anonymized token counts to Payments partner (Stripe) — no PII.

3) Cross-border considerations:
   - For US customers default execution remains inside US regions. EU/UK customers can opt for EU-only execution via our regional pinning.
   - Some control-plane metadata (non-content, e.g., metrics, routing logs) may transit between regions for orchestration but request payloads are kept in-region when regional pinning is requested.

4) Evidence items we can share: subprocessor CSV, per-model execution diagram (diagram attached), short note on retention & KV cache TTLs.

I'll attach the current subprocessor inventory and a one-page execution trajectory PDF. Connor — can you confirm the wording around telemetry (no raw payload retention) is still accurate after the recent change to prefix-caching?

Marissa
Security Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick Q — where do requests actually execute? (internal)

Marissa — quick confirm: telemetry agents publish aggregated metrics; we do not persist raw prompts/responses in Datadog. Prefix/KV cache lives on serving nodes with a TTL (default 2 hours for hosted; customers can configure). When regional pinning is enabled, caches are provisioned in the pinned region and are not replicated cross-region.

You can hand that back to Jane as: "Telemetry collects anonymized operational metrics only; no raw request payloads are stored in our observability systems. KV/prefix caches are transient and respect regional pinning."

Connor Obrien
VP, Product, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@alphahealth.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q — where do requests actually execute?

Hi Jane — attaching the inventory and a brief diagram you can share with your security reviewer. Summary below (short, copy-ready):

Summary (copy for security review):
- Default execution: requests from Alpha Health's east-coast users are routed to Redwood's US-East serving pool (us-east-1). Failover options include us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for availability.
- Subprocessors (common transient touches): FastEdge CDN (edge LB), CloudProvider (compute hosting in us-east-1), Datadog (aggregated telemetry), Stripe (billing metadata). A full CSV of subprocessors is attached.
- Cross-border: default stays within the US for US customers. If you enable EU regional pinning we confine compute and caches to EU regions; control-plane metadata (non-content routing logs) may transit for orchestration but does not contain raw prompts/responses.
- Retention and deletion: KV/prefix cache entries are transient (default TTL 2 hours) and are cleared on customer erasure requests; we do not persist raw prompts in telemetry or billing subprocessors.

Attachments: redwood-exec-trajectory-2027.pdf (diagram), subprocessor-inventory-2027.csv (current approved list).

If your reviewer needs a signed attestation or SOC2 artifact references, tell me and I will route the formal packet.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
